lines.japanese: 「ええと、山科さん」
lines.english: “Um, Yamashina.”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: 「もうそろそろ、卒業文集の製作も終わると思うんだ」
lines.english: “I think we're nearly finished with the graduation anthology.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、そうだね。長い間お世話になりました」
lines.english: “Yes, I suppose we are. Thank you for everything you've done for me over all this time.”

lines.japanese: 山科さんは片付けの手を止めて、膝の前に手を置いた。姿勢を整えて頭をぺこり。なんだか給仕のひとみたいでドキッとした。
lines.english: Yamashina stopped tidying, placed her hands before her knees, straightened her posture, and dipped her head. She looked strangely like a waitress, and my heart gave a jump.

lines.japanese: 「やめてよ、長い間って、たった三日間じゃない」
lines.english: “Don't say 'all this time.' It's only been three days.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふ、まだ終わってないしね」
lines.english: “Hee hee. And it isn't over yet.”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Right.”

lines.japanese: そうか、山科さんが参加してからまだ三日しかたってないのか。楽しかったからすぐに時間が過ぎた気もするけど、もっと長い間一緒に作業してたような気もする。
lines.english: Had it really been only three days since Yamashina joined us? Perhaps the fun had made the time fly, and yet somehow it felt as if we had been working together much longer.

lines.japanese: 僕は作業を楽しく進められたことについて、お礼を言うつもりだった。
lines.english: I had meant to thank her for making the work so much fun.

lines.japanese: 「あ、えっと、山科さんに、ちゃんとお礼を言っておきたいんだ」
lines.english: “Um... I want to make sure I thank you properly, Yamashina.”

lines.japanese: 「お礼？　なんの？」
lines.english: “Thank me? For what?”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、ここまで協力してもらったお礼って言うか、実際の作業だけじゃなくて、いろいろ……」
lines.english: “Well, for helping us get this far. And not only with the actual work. For... all sorts of things.”

lines.japanese: 言おうと思ってたことはあるんだけど、言葉にするとなると難しいものだ。かと言って、感謝してますなんて畏まった言い方で表せるようなものでもない。
lines.english: I knew what I wanted to tell her, but putting it into words was difficult. And it was not the kind of feeling I could express with anything so formal as ‘I am grateful.’

lines.japanese: 何だろうな、こういうの……何て言えばいいんだろう。
lines.english: What was it, then? What was I trying to say?

lines.japanese: 「大げさじゃない？」
lines.english: “Aren’t you making a bit much of this?”

lines.japanese: 「そうかな。そんなつもりじゃないんだけどな」
lines.english: “Am I? I didn't mean to.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふ、羽田君の言い方だと、私たちこの作業が終わったら、もう会わないように聞こえるよ」
lines.english: “Hee hee. The way you're talking, it sounds as if we'll never see each other again once this is over.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「卒業してお互い忙しくなっても、半年に一度くらいは生きてるか確認できるといいね」
lines.english: “Even after we graduate and both get busy, it would be nice if we could check that the other one's still alive every six months or so.”

lines.japanese: 山科さんの無邪気な提案に、僕は思わず言葉に詰まる。半年先まで、この世界にいられるかどうかなんて保証はない。
lines.english: Her innocent suggestion stopped the words in my throat. There was no guarantee I would still be in this world six months from now.

lines.japanese: けれど、それを無碍に否定する言葉は口に出来ない。山科さんの気持ちを曇らせるようなことは言いたくない。
lines.english: But I couldn't bring myself to reject the idea outright. I didn't want to say anything that would cast a shadow over her happiness.

lines.japanese: 「……うん。顔を見に行くよ、あの煙草屋に。生存報告と一緒に、近況とかも話したいし」
lines.english: “...Yeah. I'll come see you at that tobacco shop. We can report that we're still alive and tell each other what we've been up to.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふっ」
lines.english: “Hee hee.”

lines.japanese: 近況報告か。そんなの今までしたことないな。だって街を歩いてて同じ学校のひとを見かけても、話すきっかけがなかったから。
lines.english: Tell each other what we'd been up to... I had never done that before. Even when I spotted someone from school around town, I had never found a reason to speak to them.

lines.japanese: 「これからもよろしくね、委員長」
lines.english: “Let’s stay friends, President.”

lines.japanese: これからも。そう、これから卒業したとしても、僕たちの関係はそれで終わりじゃないんだ。
lines.english: Stay friends. That was right—even after graduation, what lay between us would not simply end.

lines.japanese: 僕たちの関係……そうか、自分でなにを言いたいか、分かった気がする。
lines.english: What lay between us... Ah. I thought I finally understood what I had been trying to say.

lines.japanese: 感謝してますでも、ありがとうございましたでもなくて、もっと僕たちの距離は……。
lines.english: It wasn’t ‘I’m grateful’ or ‘thank you very much.’ There wasn’t that kind of distance between us anymore...

lines.japanese: 「えっと」

lines.english: “Hm?”

lines.japanese: 「さんきゅ」
lines.english: “Thanks.”

lines.japanese: そう、それだ。
lines.english: Yes. That was it.

lines.japanese: 出来るだけ爽やかな表情を作って笑いかけると、山科さんは目をぱちくりとさせて僕を見つめた。
lines.english: I summoned the breeziest expression I could manage and smiled at her. Yamashina blinked several times and stared.

lines.japanese: 「なにそれ」
lines.english: “What was that?”

lines.japanese: 僕の自称・爽やかな笑顔は、みるみるだらしないものに変わっていった。でもそれでいい。山科さんもいま、同じ笑顔を浮かべてるから。
lines.english: My self-proclaimed breezy smile rapidly collapsed into a foolish grin. But that was all right. Yamashina was wearing the same grin now.

lines.japanese: 彼女は軽く吹きだしたあと、僕ら学生の等身大の笑い声をあげた。
lines.english: A tiny snort escaped her, and then she broke into the open, unguarded laughter of an ordinary girl our age.

lines.japanese: 「な、何だよ、笑わないでよ」
lines.english: “H-hey, don't laugh.”

lines.japanese: 「あはは、ごめん、ツボッちゃった」
lines.english: “Ahaha, sorry. That really got me.”

lines.japanese: 僕がずっと憧れていたもの。こんな手の届くところにあったんだ。
lines.english: The thing I had always longed for had been here, within reach, all along.

lines.japanese: 僕は残務処理の６番“クラスに友達をつくる”に済マークを付けておいた。
lines.english: I put a DONE mark beside Unfinished Business No. 6: ‘Make a friend in class.’

lines.japanese: 片付けが終わったので、僕は一人で職員室に向かっていた。
lines.english: Once we had finished cleaning up, I headed for the faculty room alone.

lines.japanese: 担任の先生に明日には終わりそうだという報告をするためと、もう一つ、針生さんのことも引っかかっていた。
lines.english: I needed to tell our homeroom teacher that the anthology would probably be finished tomorrow. But something about Hariu had been bothering me too.

lines.japanese: 職員室に呼ばれるなんて、なにがあったんだろう。針生さんは授業を休みがちだから、出席日数のことかな。
lines.english: Why had he been summoned to the faculty room? Since he missed class so often, perhaps it had something to do with his attendance.

lines.japanese: そんな考えごとに意識をとられていたから、通りがかりの教室の中から話し声が聞こえたのは、運がよかったのかもしれない。
lines.english: I was so lost in thought that it may have been sheer luck when I heard voices coming from a classroom I was passing.

lines.japanese: 「針生さん？」
lines.english: “Hariu?”

lines.japanese: 教室の中にいたのは年上の同級生と担任の恩田先生だ。何を話しているんだろう。
lines.english: Inside were my older classmate and our homeroom teacher, Ms. Onda. What could they be discussing?

lines.japanese: 聞き耳を立てるつもりはなかったけど、用事があるのはこの二人だから、職員室に行く必要もなくなってしまったので、廊下で二人の会話を立ち聞きする形になった。
lines.english: I hadn't meant to eavesdrop. But these were the two people I needed to see, which meant there was no longer any reason to go to the faculty room. And so I found myself listening from the corridor.

lines.japanese: 「はぁ、仰りたいことは分かりましたとも。ええもう、出来うる限り最善の努力は尽くしますとも、ミスお節介」
lines.english: “Yes, yes, I understand exactly what you're trying to say. I assure you I'll make every effort humanly possible, Miss Busybody.”

lines.japanese: 「針生君。あなたもずっと学校に居たいわけじゃないでしょう？　出席日数さえ足りれば卒業は出来るんです」
lines.english: “Hariu. You don't intend to remain at this school forever, do you? If you attend enough days, you can graduate.”

lines.japanese: 「努力はするって言ってんでしょう、誓約書でも書けってんですかァ。指きりげんまん、嘘ついたら針生さんお飲みいたします？」
lines.english: “I said I’d try, didn’t I? What, do you want it in writing? Pinkie swear? Cross my heart and hope to die—stick a needle in Hariu’s eye?”

lines.japanese: 針生さんと先生は、どうやら卒業できるかについて話をしているみたいだ。
lines.english: Apparently Hariu and the teacher were discussing whether he would be able to graduate.

lines.japanese: そういえば文集の製作に参加してくれてるけど、針生さん、大丈夫なのかな。
lines.english: Come to think of it, he had been helping us with the anthology, but was Hariu himself going to be all right?

lines.japanese: 「成績優秀なあなたが、どうして卒業するつもりがないのか理解に苦しみます。頑張らなくても、真面目に学校に来るだけでいいんです」
lines.english: “Your grades are excellent. I cannot understand why you have no intention of graduating. You don't even need to work hard. All you have to do is come to school regularly.”

lines.japanese: 「はン、本音を言っちゃいなさいよ、あんたはどっちだっていいんでしょう。俺が学園に残ろうと知ったこっちゃない、だけど留年者を出して何もしませんでしたじゃ困るってだけじゃないの」
lines.english: “Hah. Why don't you say what you really mean? You don't care either way. You couldn't care less if I stay here, but you can't have a student repeat the year and make it look as if you did nothing about it.”

lines.japanese: 「安心しなよ、説得はしたってことにしておけばいいじゃない。素行不良の生徒がちょいと努力が足りなかったってだけのことですよ。それに身体のことだってあるでしょう」
lines.english: “Relax. Just say you tried to persuade me. A delinquent student fell a little short on effort—that's all. And then there's my health, remember?”

lines.japanese: 「医師の診断書だって出してんです。本当なら入院しててもおかしくないんですから、こうして通えるだけでも充分じゃありません？　卒業なんて、はン、そんな大それたこと考えちゃいませんよ」
lines.english: “You've got the doctor's certificate. By rights, I could be in the hospital. Isn't it enough that I drag myself here at all? Graduation? Hah. I wouldn't dream of anything so grand.”

lines.japanese: 「今年も受験はするんでご安心を。まあ受かったって進学はしねえけど、それで合格率は上がンだ。学校にとっちゃ益になるでしょう」
lines.english: “Don't worry, I'll sit the entrance exams again this year. I won't enroll even if I pass, but another acceptance will raise your numbers. That's good for the school, isn't it?”

lines.japanese: 話の内容がぶつ切り過ぎてよく分からないけど、針生さんは卒業する意思がないってことなんだろうか。
lines.english: The conversation was too fragmented for me to make complete sense of it, but did Hariu truly have no intention of graduating?

lines.japanese: 先生も落ちついて話してはいるものの、平行線のままの会話に疲れているようにも見える。やがて何かの書類にペンでしゃっしゃと書きこんで、教室から出ていってしまった。
lines.english: The teacher spoke calmly, but she too looked tired of a conversation going nowhere. Eventually she scribbled across some document, then left the classroom.

lines.japanese: 針生さんは背中を仰けぞらせて椅子にもたれかかると、しばらくその態勢のままぎしぎしと身体を揺らして遊んでいた。
lines.english: Hariu arched his back over the chair and stayed that way for a while, amusing himself by rocking until its frame creaked beneath him.
“Mm.”

lines.japanese: 「どうも」
lines.english: “Hello.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは廊下から見られているのに気づいたみたいだ。最大限に仰けぞって、顔を逆さまにしながら僕と目を合わせた。
lines.english: He seemed to have noticed me watching from the hall. Leaning back as far as he could, he met my eyes with his face upside down.

lines.japanese: 「おまえ、いつからそこにいた」
lines.english: “How long have you been standing there?”

lines.japanese: 「ええと、先生と話していたところからです」
lines.english: “Um... since you were talking with the teacher.”

lines.japanese: 「ハッ」
lines.english: “Hah.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは体を起こして、僕にこいこいと手招きをした。知らない教室に入って彼の元へと向かう。
lines.english: Hariu sat up and crooked a finger at me. I entered the unfamiliar classroom and went over to him.

lines.japanese: 「あの、卒業がどうとかって聞こえました」
lines.english: “I heard something about graduating.”

lines.japanese: 「あん？　全部聞いてたんじゃないの」
lines.english: “Huh? Didn't you hear the whole thing?”

lines.japanese: 「ええと、入院とか出席日数って言葉が聞こえたんですけど、どこか悪いんですか？」
lines.english: “Um, I heard the words hospital and attendance. Is something wrong with you?”

lines.japanese: 「あァ」
lines.english: “Ah.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは鞄からペットボトルを取りだすと、またいつものようにきゅるっとキャップを回して、喉にぐいぐいと流しこんだ。
lines.english: Hariu took a plastic bottle from his bag, twisted off the cap with its usual little squeak, and took several long gulps.

lines.japanese: 「俺なァ、あと何年生きられるか分からないらしい」
lines.english: “Apparently nobody knows how many more years I've got.”
“What?!”

lines.japanese: 僕が大きな声を出すと、針生さんはチッチと口の前で人差し指を揺らして、お静かにと言葉を添えた。
lines.english: At my outburst, Hariu went tsk-tsk, wagged an index finger before his lips, and added, ‘Quiet, please.’

lines.japanese: 「そ、それって大きな病気なんですか」
lines.english: “I-is it something serious?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、見ての通り至って健康だねえ。いつ爆弾が破裂するか分からないだけで、あるいはジジイになるまで五体無事かもしンねえしな」
lines.english: “No. As you can see, I’m the picture of health. Nobody knows when the bomb will go off, that’s all. Then again, I might make it to a ripe old age in one piece.”

lines.japanese: 「それなら、その、入院とかしてもらったり、手術とか……」
lines.english: “But then, couldn't you be admitted to a hospital, or have surgery, or...”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、そこンとこは俺の好きにさせてもらってるよ。もし先がないなら、一分一秒すら無駄には出来ないでしょう」
lines.english: “Well, they've let me have my way on that score. If I haven't got long, I can hardly afford to waste a minute or a second of it.”

lines.japanese: 「ある日朝起きたらぽっくり逝ってましたなんて、そんなドラマチックな話じゃないしなァ。その時がくりゃア、だらだらベッドの上で寝たきりンなって、さよなら天国また来て地獄」
lines.english: “It isn’t some dramatic story where I wake up dead one morning. When the time comes, I’ll be stuck in bed, lingering on. Bye-bye, heaven. Hello again, hell.”

lines.japanese: 「どうせなら、やりたいことは全部やっといた方がいいだろ。別に感傷的な話じゃない、俺がそうしたいってだけのことだ」
lines.english: “So I might as well do everything I want while I can, right? It’s not some sentimental thing. It’s just what I want to do.”

lines.japanese: 僕は針生さんが生きいそぐように知識や情報を追いもとめている理由がやっと分かった。
lines.english: At last I understood why Hariu pursued knowledge and information as if he were racing through his life.

lines.japanese: 「でもそれなら、卒業はした方がいいんじゃないですか。社会人の方が何かと便利でしょう」
lines.english: “But in that case, shouldn't you graduate? Life would be more convenient as a working adult.”

lines.japanese: 「そうかァ？　なあ羽田、学生生活が三年間しかないのって、そっちの方が勿体ないと思わねえ？」
lines.english: “Would it? Tell me, Haneda, don't you think it's more of a waste that student life lasts only three years?”

lines.japanese: 「おまえも許されンなら、いつまでも学生を続けたいと思わねえ？　なにかと便利だろ」
lines.english: “If you could, wouldn’t you want to stay a student forever too? Makes life easier, right?”

lines.japanese: 言われてみれば、僕は社会に出たいなんて思ったこともないし、出て何をしようかなんて考えたこともない。
lines.english: Now that he mentioned it, I had never wanted to go out into the working world, nor had I ever considered what I might do once I did.

lines.japanese: 山科さんがいつか言っていた。大学に行けば、社会に出る猶予が四年もらえる。つまりそういうことだ。
lines.english: Yamashina had once said that going to university bought you another four years before you had to face the working world. So that was what he meant.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ卒業はしたくないんですか？」
lines.english: “Then you don't want to graduate?”

lines.japanese: 「どっちでもいい。してもしなくても大差ないしな。このまま３０、４０まで学生やってるのも一興だ。どうせ学園側は俺を放りだせない」
lines.english: “I don't care either way. It makes precious little difference. Staying a student into my thirties or forties might be amusing. The school can't throw me out, after all.”

lines.japanese: 「それって、さっき話してた合格率って言葉と関係あるんですか」
lines.english: “Does that have something to do with what you said about their acceptance rate?”

lines.japanese: 「ハハ、おまえにしちゃ察しがいいな。去年のパンフに載ってる合格者発表を見てみろ、何人俺がいるか分からない」
lines.english: “Ha ha. Sharp of you for once. Look at the list of successful applicants in last year’s prospectus. There’s no telling how many times you’ll find my name.”

lines.japanese: 僕は針生さんの言っていることが理解できた。つまり学園側としても、真面目に説得する気はないってことだ。
lines.english: I understood what Hariu meant. In other words, the school had no sincere desire to persuade him either.

lines.japanese: 「でも、なにかが違いますよ。とにかく針生さんは卒業するべきです」
lines.english: “Still, something about this is wrong. Whatever else happens, you ought to graduate.”

lines.japanese: 「んン？　どうした急に。精神的に貧困にでもなったか」
lines.english: “Hmm? What's come over you? Suddenly stricken with poverty of spirit?”

lines.japanese: 僕の論理的じゃない論理展開に、彼は口の端を吊りあげた。だけど立ち去りはしない。以前だったらここで話は終わっていたはずだ。
lines.english: The corner of his mouth curled at my thoroughly illogical line of reasoning. But he did not leave. Once, our conversation would have ended there.

lines.japanese: 短い期間だけど一緒に放課後の時間を過ごしているうち、僕は青臭い理想論に耳を貸してもらえるぐらい、針生さんの関心を買うことができたのだろうか。
lines.english: We had spent only a little time together after school. Even so, perhaps I had earned enough of Hariu's interest that he would lend an ear to my callow idealism.

lines.japanese: 「針生さんの気持ちは分かります──」
lines.english: “I understand how you feel—”

lines.japanese: 僕は続けた。
lines.english: I went on.

lines.japanese: 「──分かると思います。だって、実はおれも、いついなくなるか分からない身なんです」
lines.english: “—or I think I do. The truth is, I don't know when I might disappear either.”

lines.japanese: 僕なんかの話を聞いてくれる針生さんに、嘘はつきたくない。だけどもちろん本当のことは言えない。僕は唇を湿らせながら、慎重に言葉を選んでいた。
lines.english: I did not want to lie to Hariu when he had been willing to hear me out. But of course, I couldn't tell him the truth. Wetting my lips, I chose my words with care.

lines.japanese: 「おれ、卒業したらふるさとへ帰るつもりなんです。そこはとても遠い国で、もうこっちには戻ってこられないかもしれ──」
lines.english: “After graduation, I mean to return to my homeland. It's a country very far away, and I may never be able to come back—”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　それはもしかして、陛下やハヤブサとも関係あることか？」
lines.english: “Hm? Does this have something to do with His Majesty and Hayabusa?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 陛下、ハヤブサ……とかはよく分からないけど、針生さんの表情を見れば、僕の言葉に明らかな興味を寄せてきたのは分かる。
lines.english: His Majesty? Hayabusa? I didn’t know what either meant, but one look at Hariu’s face told me that my words had unmistakably caught his interest.

lines.japanese: 信じてもらえないと思ってたのに、彼は信じてくれた。その目はまるで、獲物が息絶えるのを待っている獣のようだ。
lines.english: I had expected him not to believe me, yet he did. His eyes were those of a beast waiting for its quarry to breathe its last.

lines.japanese: 「羽田は自分たちの存在があやふやなことに気づいてンのか？　いや、違うよな、つっても下手は打てない……」
lines.english: “Has Haneda realized how uncertain their existence is? No, that can't be it. Still, I can't afford a false move...”

lines.japanese: 早口で何事か呟いている。もしかしたら彼は何か知っているんだろうか。今度は僕が待つ番だった。
lines.english: He was muttering something too quickly for me to follow. Could he know something? Now it was my turn to wait.

lines.japanese: 「どういうことだ？」
lines.english: “What exactly do you mean?”

lines.japanese: 「はい。もともと僕は、ここにいるべき人間じゃないんです」
lines.english: “Well... I was never someone who belonged here in the first place.”

lines.japanese: 「多元世界の真実ってやつか」
lines.english: “The truth of the multiverse, is that it?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ！」
lines.english: “What?!”

lines.japanese: やっぱり針生さんは何か知っているんだ。僕は思わず身を乗りだした。
lines.english: Hariu did know something. I leaned eagerly toward him before I could stop myself.

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、じゃあ、グレタガルド……のことも？」
lines.english: “Th-then do you know about Gretagard too?”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは首肯するように顎を引いた。
lines.english: Hariu lowered his chin in what seemed to be a nod.

lines.japanese: 僕は息を呑んだ。針生さんはふたたび表情を横向けて、独り言をもらす。
lines.english: I caught my breath. Hariu turned his face aside again and murmured to himself.

lines.japanese: 「へえ、こいつは偶然なのか、潜在的に意識があったのか……考えることはみな同じってわけか、面白いねェ」
lines.english: “Well, now. Is this mere coincidence, or was there some awareness buried beneath the surface...? I suppose everyone arrives at the same ideas. How interesting.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、なんです？」
lines.english: “What was that?”

lines.japanese: 僕は聞きかえしたが、彼はさらに質問で返してきた。
lines.english: I asked him to repeat himself. He answered with another question.

lines.japanese: 「なにおまえ、いつ消えんの」
lines.english: “So when are you going to disappear?”

lines.japanese: 「はあ、おそらくは卒業するのと同時だと思いますけど」
lines.english: “Well... probably when I graduate.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは腕を組んで考えはじめた。渡来さん、山科さん、そしていま針生さんも。いままで誰も信じてくれなかった話を、どうしてみんな簡単に信じてくれるんだろう。
lines.english: Hariu folded his arms and began to think. Watarai, Yamashina, and now Hariu. Why did all of them so readily believe a story no one had ever believed before?

lines.japanese: 泣きたくなってきた。もしこのひとたちにもっと早く会えていたら、僕は向こうの世界へ行くことを拒んでいたかもしれない。
lines.english: I felt close to tears. If I had met these people sooner, perhaps I would have refused to go to the other world.

lines.japanese: 「おまえ、この世界でやり残したことはねえの」
lines.english: “Is there nothing you've left undone in this world?”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: この世界でやり残したこと……僕は携帯電話の中の自己目標と、卒業文集制作のことを思いだした。
lines.english: Something left undone in this world... I thought of the personal goals stored in my phone, and of the graduation anthology.

lines.japanese: この生涯の『残務処理』が終わったら、未練なんてないはずだった。
lines.english: Once I had finished the ‘Unfinished Business’ of this life, I was supposed to have no regrets.

lines.japanese: そうだと思っていた。
lines.english: That was what I had believed.

lines.japanese: 「あの、おれは……」
「ああ、悪い。べつにおまえの人生相談にまで乗ってやる気はないよ。やることなけりゃ消えりゃあいい」
lines.english: “Ah, sorry. I have no intention of becoming your life counselor too. If you've got nothing to do, go ahead and disappear.”

lines.japanese: 「でも、まァ、俺は死ぬまでに興味あることは全てやっとくけどな。ハハ、おまえみたいにいじけた子供にはなりたくないからなァ」
lines.english: “Me, I'll do everything that interests me before I die. Ha ha. I'd hate to turn into a sulking child like you.”

lines.japanese: 「いじけた……」
lines.english: “A sulking child...”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあな。また明日」
lines.english: “See you tomorrow.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんは鞄を提げて帰ってしまった。ひとり残された僕は、担任への報告のため職員室へ向かう。
lines.english: Hariu picked up his bag and left. Alone once more, I continued to the faculty room to make my report to our homeroom teacher.

lines.japanese: 帰り道、僕は歩道橋の上でケータイの画面を眺めていた。
lines.english: On the way home, I stood on the pedestrian bridge and gazed at my phone.

lines.japanese: 残務処理の全項目に『済』マークが付いている。我ながらよく為しとげたものだ。
lines.english: Every item of my Unfinished Business bore a DONE mark. I had done rather well, if I said so myself.

lines.japanese: 未練はないはずなんだ。僕の空っぽな物語は、この数行の中で完結を遂げたんだ。
lines.english: I was supposed to have no regrets. The empty story of my life had reached its conclusion within those few lines.

lines.japanese: これで満足なんだ。
lines.english: I was satisfied.

lines.japanese: これで満足なはずなんだ。
lines.english: I ought to have been satisfied.

lines.japanese: だけどちっとも嬉しくなかった。
lines.english: And yet I wasn't happy in the least.

lines.japanese: 僕はいま自分が為すべきことを考えてみた。
lines.english: I tried to think what I ought to do now.

lines.japanese: 明日には完成する予定の卒業文集。自分の意思で始めたわけじゃない。むしろ逃げだしてしまいたかった。
lines.english: The graduation anthology was due to be finished tomorrow. I hadn't begun it of my own will. If anything, I had wanted to run away from it.

lines.japanese: けれど、いまこれを投げだして旅立つのだとしたら、それは僕にとって未練だ。
lines.english: And yet, if I abandoned it now and departed, it would become a lingering regret.

lines.japanese: そうだ、それさえ完成すれば思いのこすことなんてないはずだ。
lines.english: Yes. Once that was complete, surely there would be nothing left to regret.

lines.japanese: そのためには、針生さんに卒業してもらわないといけない。３－Ａ全員の卒業文が載らない卒業文集だなんて、そんなものは僕の思いえがく完成形じゃない。
lines.english: For that to happen, Hariu would have to graduate. An anthology without a piece from every member of Class 3-A could never be the finished work I had imagined.

lines.japanese: 僕はメモ帳画面に新たな一行を付けくわえた。
lines.english: I added one more line to the notepad on my phone.

lines.japanese: “７：卒業文集を完成させる”
lines.english: 7. Complete the graduation anthology.
